draft.title: Individual and collective experience
card: an experience that belongs to one person, such as grief, ambition or a private choice. The text stays close to that person's thoughts and feelings.
an experience shared by a group, such as war, migration or a community's loss. The text shows what many people live through, not only one.
Many texts show both. A writer may follow one character to show how a shared event touches a single life.
To tell them apart, ask whose experience the text is mainly about: one person's, or a group's.
draft.remember: Individual experience is one person's. Collective experience is shared by a group.

a.q: Which example is mainly a collective experience?
opts: A town mourning the loss of its main employer
A teenager nervous before a solo audition
A man regretting a harsh word to his brother
A student set on becoming a surgeon
a.why: A whole town facing a loss is an experience many people share. The other three focus on one person's private feelings or goals, even though others may feel something similar.
a.clue: Which one happens to a group, not one person?

b.q: A short story follows Lena, who leaves her village with many other families to settle in Australia. It shows the journey through her fears and memories. What does the story show?
opts: A collective experience, seen through one person
Only an individual experience, because Lena narrates
Only a collective experience, because Lena has no feelings
Neither, because migration is not a human experience
b.why: Many families make the same journey, so migration is shared. The story uses Lena's fears and memories to show it. Choosing one character does not make the experience purely individual.
b.clue: Many families travel, but we see it through one person.

a.best: A town mourning the loss of its main employer

b.best: A collective experience, seen through one person

problems.detail: The clue 'Many families travel, but we see it through one person' almost repeats the correct option 'A collective experience, seen through one person', so it gives the answer away.
Two distractors are implausible for Year 12. 'Lena has no feelings' contradicts the stem, and 'migration is not a human experience' is absurd. This leaves a near-trivial choice between two options.
